prerequisites: Descriptive Geometry and Technical Drawing (1) and (2)
Ability to create the execution drawing of a machine part, to create an assembly drawing of a mechanical structure, to identify the component elements of an assembly/subassembly and its drawing.

learning_outcomes.text: Identify and describe basic principles and methods of the mechanical engineering domain.

Know and explain categories of dimensions and limit deviations, dimensional tolerances and fits (graphic representation, notation on drawings, selection), macro and micro-geometric form deviations, orientation and relative position deviations of surfaces.
Explain types of tolerances and fits for specific mechanical engineering joints (bearing assemblies, conical assemblies, threaded assemblies, parallel key and disc key assemblies).
Know the methods and universal means for controlling linear dimensions of simple-shaped parts in mechanical assembly structures.
Define fundamental notions related to dimensional and geometric tolerances.
Know categories of dimensions and limit deviations, dimensional tolerances and fits.
Apply criteria, evaluation methods, concepts, theories, and programs in the design of mechanical systems.

Apply knowledge in graphic representation, notation on drawings, and selection of specifications for the studied domain of macro and micro-geometric form deviations, orientation and relative position deviations of surfaces.
Know and explain types of tolerances and fits for specific mechanical engineering joints (bearing assemblies, conical assemblies, threaded assemblies, parallel key and disc key assemblies).
Compare different methods and universal means for controlling linear dimensions of simple-shaped parts in mechanical assembly structures.
Select and analyze specific bibliographic sources in the mechanical engineering domain.
Operate with basic methods and techniques in the field and associate them with specific graphic representations of the mechanical engineering domain.
Develop technical documentation, including assembly execution drawings, interpret technical conditions, and verify consistency between prescribed characteristics and the functional role of parts.
Understand the use of different measurement methods and corresponding measuring instruments.
Operate with laboratory measuring instruments used for measuring dimensional and geometric characteristics.
Critically evaluate methods and equipment in the field of dimensional control using specific evaluation instruments and methods.

Respect ethical principles, norms, and values in the correct and timely execution of professional tasks, by adopting a rigorous, efficient, and responsible work strategy in decision-making for problem-solving.

Integrate into a work group, assuming specific roles and achieving good communication within the team, apply techniques for team coordination and relationship building, to work in a team and accept diversity of opinions.
Execute professional tasks according to specified requirements and within imposed deadlines, following a pre-established work plan and under qualified guidance.
Continuously inform and document themselves in their own field of activity by adequately using efficient lifelong learning methods and techniques.

syllabus_topics: Introduction (Object and importance of the discipline; Principle of interchangeability in mechanical engineering; aspects related to its observance in design, execution, and operation of machines)

Dimensional precision (Dimensions, categories of dimensions, limit deviations, dimensional tolerance, graphic representations, notation on part drawings; Fit, types of fits, limit clearances and interferences in joints, fit systems, fit tolerance, graphic representations, notation of fits on assembly drawings; Characteristics of the ISO system of tolerances and fits, selection of tolerances and fits for machine parts and mechanical assemblies)

Precision of surface form (Macro-geometric form deviations; defining deviations from straightness, flatness, circularity, cylindricity, given profile shape, given surface shape, graphic representations, notation of form tolerances on drawings; Waviness and surface roughness; causes of their occurrence, characteristics, physical and statistical parameters of roughness, inscription on drawings)

Precision of orientation and relative position of surfaces (Orientation deviations: deviation from parallelism, deviation from inclination, deviation from perpendicularity; cases, definition, graphic representations, inscription of orientation tolerances on drawings; Relative position deviations of surfaces: deviations from coaxiality and concentricity, deviation from symmetry, deviation from nominal position; definition, graphic representation, inscription of relative position tolerances on drawings; Radial runout and frontal runout; types of radial and frontal runouts, graphic representations, inscription of runout tolerances on drawings)

Dimension chains (Categories of dimensions in dimension chains, classification of dimension chains; Direct problem of solving dimension chains, solution methods; Inverse problem of solving dimension chains, solution methods)
Tolerances and fits for bearing assemblies (Tolerance fields for bearing mounting dimensions; Fits for bearing assemblies, their notation on assembly drawings)

Tolerances of smooth conical surfaces (Dimensional elements of smooth conical surfaces, methods of dimensioning conical surfaces; Methods of tolerancing smooth conical surfaces, inscription of conical surface tolerances on part drawings)

Tolerances and fits for threaded assemblies (Dimensional elements of threaded surfaces, pitch and angle deviations, their influences on the mean diameter; Tolerances and fits for general purpose ISO metric threads, their notation on drawings)
Tolerances and fits for key assemblies (Dimensional elements of parallel key and disc key assemblies; Fits for parallel key and disc key assemblies, their notation on assembly drawings)

Dimensional control methods and means (Classification of dimensional control methods, metrological characteristics; Universal dimensional control means: slip gauges, linear vernier instruments, micrometric screw instruments, comparator devices; Measurement errors: definition, classification criteria)

Control of linear dimensions for simple-shaped parts (Control of external dimensions (external diameters, heights, thicknesses) with universal measuring instruments; Control of internal dimensions (internal diameters, depths) with universal measuring instruments)
Control of macro-geometric form of surfaces (Control of deviations from straightness and flatness; Control of deviations from circularity; Control of deviations from the given shape of surfaces)

Control of orientation and relative position of surfaces (Control of deviations from parallelism and perpendicularity; Control of deviations from coaxiality and concentricity; Control of deviations from symmetry; Control of radial runout and frontal runout)

Occupational safety for laboratory activities in "Tolerances and Dimensional Control" (Occupational safety briefing, student registration, presentation of the laboratory and laboratory works; Presentation of universal measuring instruments (slip gauges, calipers, micrometers, comparator instruments) used in laboratory works)

Control of external and internal dimensions with linear vernier instruments, micrometric screw instruments and comparator instruments (Measurement of external and internal dimensions with calipers; Measurement of external and internal dimensions with micrometers; Measurement of external and internal dimensions with comparator instruments)

Control of macrometric form deviations of surfaces (Verification of straightness by the light gap method and measurement of deviation from straightness with indicator instrument; Measurement of deviation from flatness with indicator instrument; Measurement of deviations from circularity for external and internal cylindrical surfaces with comparator instruments)

Control of orientation and relative position deviations of surfaces (Measurement of deviations from parallelism in plane and space; Verification of coaxiality with control mandrels; Measurement of deviation from concentricity; Measurement of deviation from symmetry; Measurement of radial runout and frontal runout)

Use of ISO standards for calculations with ISO tolerances and fits (Identification of elements defining a tolerated dimension; Establishing (with the help of standards) limit deviations for a shaft and a bore, graphical representation of limit deviations and tolerance zones for shafts and bores, calculating the tolerance of a dimension; Identification of fit type and fit system in which a given fit is established, graphical representation of the fit, determination of limit clearances or interferences in a joint, calculating the tolerance of a fit; Inscription of dimensional tolerances on part drawings and fits on assembly drawings)
Solving dimension chains (Solving the direct problem by the algebraic method; Solving the direct problem by the maximum and minimum method; Solving the direct problem by the probabilistic method)

Final verification and grading (Completion of laboratory reports for performed laboratory works; Re-doing an unperformed laboratory work; Verification of reports and final grading of students for laboratory activity)
teaching_methods: Oral exposition of notions, accompanied by graphical representations, measurement schemes, and demonstrations on the board.
Presentation of mechanical components and elementary information about them.
Solving numerical applications at the end of each course.
Occupational safety briefing for laboratory activities.
Discussions with students on laboratory reports.
Discussion of control methods, measurement schemes, necessary control equipment, and measurement techniques.
Presentation of measuring instrument structures and their usage.
Decision-making on controlled parts (admitted/rejected) based on measurement results.

assessment_methods.method: Final colloquium (3 numerical applications, 2 theoretical subjects)

assessment_rules: The final grade results from the scores and weights allocated to each activity. Integer grades from 10 to 1 will be awarded, with grade 5 certifying the acquisition of minimal learning outcomes and the award of corresponding study credits. Conditions for passing include: using the ISO dimensional tolerance standard, identifying fit types and fit systems, calculating limit clearances/interferences and fit tolerance; solving the direct problem of dimension chains using algebraic and maximum/minimum methods; measuring a tolerated dimension with universal instruments and making a correct decision regarding the controlled part in accordance with the prescribed tolerance.
